classification.difficultyReason: Read the side, parallel and angle markings and match them to quadrilateral definitions. The square-like figure requires recognising that equal sides alone establish a rhombus, while the marked angles in (e) support the same classification.

content.prompt: Name these special quadrilaterals using the most appropriate definition.

spec.description: Upright square-shaped outline with all four sides labelled 3 cm and no angle markers.
spec.mathematics: Four equal sides establish a rhombus. Square classification additionally requires right angles, which are not marked.
spec.answerVisibility: Side measurements are permanent givens; the supplied name is hidden.

answer.worked: Rhombus: all four sides are $3\text{ cm}$. No right angles are marked, so the given information does not establish that it is a square.

spec.description: Horizontal rectangle with four right-angle squares, single ticks on horizontal sides and double ticks on vertical sides.
spec.mathematics: Four right angles establish a rectangle; opposite sides have matching equality marks.
spec.answerVisibility: All marks are permanent givens; the supplied name is hidden.

answer.worked: Rectangle: all four angles are right angles, and opposite sides are equal.

spec.description: Trapezium with matching parallel arrows on its horizontal bases and matching equality ticks on its sloping sides.
spec.mathematics: The marked parallel pair establishes a trapezium; its nonparallel sides are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: All marks are permanent givens; the supplied name is hidden.

answer.worked: Trapezium: the top and bottom sides are parallel. The matching side ticks also show that it is an isosceles trapezium.

spec.description: Tilted kite with adjacent top and right sides labelled 5 m and adjacent left and bottom sides labelled 8 m.
spec.mathematics: Two distinct pairs of adjacent equal sides establish a kite.
spec.answerVisibility: All four lengths are permanent givens; the supplied name is hidden.

answer.worked: Kite: two adjacent sides are $5\text{ m}$ each, and the other two adjacent sides are $8\text{ m}$ each.

spec.description: Slanted quadrilateral with alternating 59° and 121° interior angles and matching single ticks on all four sides.
spec.mathematics: Four matching side ticks establish a rhombus; the alternating opposite angles are consistent with a parallelogram.
spec.answerVisibility: All angles and four source ticks remain visible; the source answer is replaced only in controlled answer content.

answer.worked: All four sides have matching equality marks, so the quadrilateral is a rhombus.

spec.description: Slanted parallelogram with matching single parallel arrows on horizontal sides and matching double arrows on sloping sides.
spec.mathematics: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
spec.answerVisibility: Parallel marks are permanent givens; the supplied name is hidden.

answer.worked: Parallelogram: both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

spec.description: Horizontal rectangle with four right-angle squares and no length marks.
spec.mathematics: Four right angles establish a rectangle.
spec.answerVisibility: Right-angle marks are permanent givens; the supplied name is hidden.

answer.worked: Rectangle: all four angles are right angles.

spec.description: Shallow slanted rhombus with every side labelled 21 m, opposite acute angles labelled 27° and opposite obtuse angles labelled 153°; external angle leaders retained.
spec.mathematics: Four equal sides establish a rhombus. Alternating 27° and 153° angles agree with its shallow orientation.
spec.answerVisibility: All repeated lengths and angles remain permanent givens; the supplied name is hidden.

answer.worked: Rhombus: all four sides are $21\text{ m}$. Its angles are $27^{\circ}$ and $153^{\circ}$, so it is not a square.
